title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: 《简·爱》是英国维多利亚时代著名女作家夏洛蒂·勃朗特于 1847 年出版的长篇小说代表作。故事讲述了孤儿简·爱在舅妈家饱受虐待、在洛伍德慈善学校经历艰难成长后，前往桑菲尔德庄园担任家庭教师。她与性格孤傲却内心深情的庄园主罗切斯特先生相爱。在婚礼当天，简·爱得知罗切斯特在阁楼关押着患有疯病的合法妻子伯莎·梅森。出于对自身尊严与道德原则的坚守，简·爱毅然孤身离开。经历贫困与磨难后，简·爱继承了遗产，并在桑菲尔德庄园被毁、罗切斯特双目失明残疾后重新回到他身边，缔结了平等尊重的真挚婚姻。

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Gateshead Hall and the Red-Room
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 1 章：盖茨黑德庄园与红房子虐待

paragraphs.en: There was no possibility of taking a walk that day. We had been wandering, indeed, in the leafless shrubbery an hour in the morning; but since dinner the cold winter wind had brought with it clouds so sombre, and a rain so penetrating, that further outdoor exercise was now out of the question. I was glad of it: I never liked long walks, especially on chilly afternoons, returning home in the raw twilight, with nipped fingers and toes, and a heart humbled by the perpetual scoldings of Bessie, the nurse, and humbled by the consciousness of my physical inferiority to John, Eliza, and Georgiana Reed.
paragraphs.zh: 那天不可能出去散步了。早上我们在没有叶子的灌木丛里游荡了一个小时；但自午饭以来，寒冷的冬风带来了阴沉的乌云和穿透性的雨水，再进行室外活动是不可能的了。我为此感到高兴：我从来不喜欢长途散步，特别是在寒冷的下午，在原始的黄昏中回到家，手指和脚趾冻得发麻，而且因为保姆贝西永无休止的训斥以及自己意识到在身体上不如约翰、伊丽莎与乔治安娜·里德而心怀自卑。

paragraphs.en: I mounted into the window-seat of the breakfast-room, gathering my feet up under me, and sitting cross-legged, like a Turk. Drawing the red moreen curtain nearly close, I was enshrined in double retirement. Folds of scarlet drapery shut in my view to the right hand; to the left were the clear panes of glass, protecting, but not separating me from the drear November day. At intervals, while turning over the leaves of Bewick's History of British Birds, I studied the aspect of that winter afternoon. Far off, it offered a pale blank of mist and cloud; near a scene of wet lawn and storm-beat shrub, with an ceaseless rain sweeping wildly aslant before a long and lamentable blast.
paragraphs.zh: 我爬进早餐室的窗台盘腿坐着，把脚收在身下，像个土耳其人一样。把红色的莫林窗帘几乎拉拢，我被尊奉在双重的隐退中。深红色的帘褶封锁了我右手边的视野；左边是清澈的玻璃窗，保护着我但没有把我与沉闷的十一月时光隔开。在翻阅毕威克《英国鸟类史》的空隙，我研究着那个冬天下午的景象。远方呈现出一片苍白的雾气与乌云；近处是一片湿漉漉的草坪和狂风敲打的灌木，在一阵漫长而哀怨的狂风前，无休止的雨水狂乱地斜扫着。

paragraphs.en: My cruel cousin John Reed soon tracked me down. He bullied me daily, striking me without provocation and calling me a dependent orphan who had no right to live with his family. When he threw a heavy book at my head, cutting my scalp, the long-repressed fury exploded within me. I flew at him like a desperate wildcat. His sisters ran screaming to Mrs. Reed, who instantly commanded her maids to drag me to the dreaded Red-Room—the dark, icy chamber where my uncle Reed had died nine years before.
paragraphs.zh: 我残酷的表哥约翰·里德很快追踪到了我。他每天都霸凌我，毫无理由地殴打我，叫我无依无靠的孤儿，说我没有权利和他家住在一起。当他拿一本沉重的书砸向我的头部砸破我的头皮时，长期压抑的怒火在我心中爆发了。我像一只绝望的野猫一样扑向他。他的姐妹们尖叫着跑向里德太太，后者立刻命令她的女佣们把我拖到令人胆寒的红房子里（那是九年前我里德舅舅去世的黑暗冰冷房间）。

paragraphs.en: Locked in the cold, brooding silence of the Red-Room, terror seized my young soul. As dusk deepened, a beam of light glided across the wall, and I believed it to be the herald of a ghost. I shrieked in agony and beat my fists against the door, begging for mercy. Mrs. Reed coldly refused to let me out, and I collapsed onto the floor in a deep swoon.
paragraphs.zh: 被锁在红房子冰冷阴郁的寂静中，恐怖抓住了我年轻的灵魂。随着黄昏加深，一束光线划过墙壁，我相信那是幽灵的前兆。我在痛苦中尖叫，用拳头敲打着门，恳求宽恕。里德太太冰冷地拒绝让我出去，我在深度昏厥中倒在了地板上。

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Lowood School and Helen Burns
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 2 章：洛伍德学校与海伦·麦克风的坚忍

paragraphs.en: Following my illness, Mrs. Reed eagerly arranged to send me away to Lowood Institution, a charitable boarding school for orphan girls. The treasurer of the school, Mr. Brocklehurst, was a cold, tyrannical hypocrite who preached austerity while his own family lived in luxury. At Lowood, eighty girls suffered under freezing temperatures, burnt porridge, and harsh discipline.
paragraphs.zh: 在我生病后，里德太太迫不及待地安排把我送到洛伍德学校（一家孤儿女孩慈善寄宿学校）。学校的财务主管布洛克赫斯特先生是一个冰冷专横的伪善者，他在自己家人生活奢华的同时宣扬苦行。在洛伍德，八十个女孩在冰冻的温度、烧焦的麦片粥和严酷的纪律下受苦。

paragraphs.en: Yet at Lowood I found two souls who gave me hope: Miss Temple, the sweet and dignified superintendent, and Helen Burns, a pious, thoughtful student older than myself. Helen bore the unjust punishments of strict teachers with stoic patience and quiet grace. When I wept over being falsely branded a liar by Mr. Brocklehurst, Helen comforted me, teaching me that self-respect and spiritual integrity were far more valuable than the praise of selfish mortals.
paragraphs.zh: 然而在洛伍德我发现了两个给我希望的灵魂：泰姆普尔小姐（甜美尊严的监督员）与海伦·麦克风（一位比我年长、虔诚深沉的学生）。海伦带着坚忍的耐心与安静的优雅忍受着严厉老师的不公正惩罚。当我因被布洛克赫斯特先生冤枉为谎言家而哭泣时，海伦安慰着我，教导我自尊与精神正直远比自私凡人的赞扬更有价值。

paragraphs.en: When a devastating typhus epidemic swept through Lowood during the damp spring, dozens of girls fell ill and died. Helen, already weakened by consumption, grew mortally sick. One night, I snuck into Miss Temple's room where Helen lay dying. I wrapped my arms around her neck, and she whispered softly: 'I am going home to my Father, Jane. Do not grieve.' When I awoke the next morning, my head was resting on Helen's shoulder, and her sweet soul had fled to heaven.
paragraphs.zh: 当一场毁灭性的伤寒流行病在潮湿的春天席卷洛伍德时，几十个女孩患病死去。已经被肺病削弱的海伦病入膏肓。一天晚上，我溜进泰姆普尔小姐的房间，海伦正躺在那里濒死。我用手臂环绕着她的脖子，她软软地低语：“我要回家去见我的父了，简。不要悲伤。”当我第二天早上醒来时，我的头正靠在海伦的肩膀上，而她甜美的灵魂已经飞向了天堂。

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Arrival at Thornfield Hall
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 3 章：到达桑菲尔德庄园

paragraphs.en: Six years passed as a student and two as a teacher at Lowood. When Miss Temple married and left, I felt an overwhelming longing for freedom and a wider world. I placed an advertisement in the newspaper seeking a position as a private governess. Soon, I received a favorable reply from Mrs. Fairfax, the housekeeper of Thornfield Hall near Millcote.
paragraphs.zh: 在洛伍德作为学生度过了六年，作为老师度过了两年。当泰姆普尔小姐结婚离开后，我感受到了对自由与更广阔世界的压倒性渴望。我在报纸上刊登了一则寻找私人家庭教师职位的广告。很快，我收到了来自米尔科特附近桑菲尔德庄园管家费尔法克斯太太的赞许回复。

paragraphs.en: Arriving at Thornfield Hall on a gloomy autumn evening, I was greeted warmly by Mrs. Fairfax. The house was an ancient, stately mansion with dark oak paneling, battlements, and long corridors filled with oil paintings. My pupil was Adele Varens, a lively seven-year-old French girl who was the ward of the master of the house, Mr. Edward Rochester. Life at Thornfield was peaceful and orderly, yet a strange atmosphere hovered over the third floor.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个阴暗的秋日夜晚到达桑菲尔德庄园，我受到了费尔法克斯太太的热情招呼。这座房子是一座古老庄严的豪宅，配有深色橡木墙板、城墙以及挂满油画的长走廊。我的学生是阿黛尔·瓦伦斯，一个活泼的七岁法国女孩，她是庄园主人爱德华·罗切斯特先生的受监护人。桑菲尔德的生活和平有序，然而一种奇怪的氛围萦绕在三楼之上。

paragraphs.en: One afternoon, while walking along the third-floor corridor, I heard a sound that chilled my blood—a low, slow, mirthless laugh echoing from behind a locked door. Mrs. Fairfax assured me it was merely Grace Poole, a eccentric seamstress who worked in the attic. Yet the eerie laughter returned night after night, haunting my dreams.
paragraphs.zh: 一天下午，当沿着三楼走廊散步时，我听到了一个让我血液发凉的声音——一个低沉、缓慢、毫无欢笑意味的笑声从锁着的门后回荡。费尔法克斯太太向我保证那仅仅是格雷斯·普尔（一位在阁楼工作的古怪缝纫女工）。然而怪诞的笑声一夜又一夜重现，萦绕在我的梦中。

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Mr. Rochester and the Mysterious Laughter
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 4 章：罗切斯特先生与夜半怪笑

paragraphs.en: On a frosty January afternoon, while walking to Hay to post a letter, I heard the thundering clip-clop of a horse on the icy road. Suddenly, the horse slipped on a patch of ice, throwing its rider to the ground with a harsh curse. I stepped forward to offer assistance to the traveler, a dark-featured man with a stern, heavy brow and grim lips. He leaned heavily on my shoulder to remount his horse, unaware that I was the new governess at his estate.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个霜冻的元月下午，当步行前往海伊寄信时，我听到了马匹在冰冷道路上雷鸣般的马蹄声。突然，马匹在一块冰面上滑倒，将骑手抛到地上并伴随着一句严厉的咒骂。我走上前去向旅行者提供帮助，那是一位皮肤较黑的人，带着严厉沉重的眉宇与冷酷的双唇。他重重地靠在我的肩膀上重新骑上马，没有意识到我就是他庄园里的新家庭教师。

paragraphs.en: Returning to Thornfield, I learned that the stranger was none other than Mr. Edward Rochester, the master of the hall. In the days that followed, Mr. Rochester summoned me to the drawing-room in the evenings. Though dark, imperious, and sarcastic, he conversed with me as an intellectual equal, probing my thoughts and respecting my candid, independent answers.
paragraphs.zh: 回到桑菲尔德，我得知这位陌生人不是别人，正是庄园的主人爱德华·罗切斯特先生。在随后的日子里，罗切斯特先生在晚上召我到客厅。虽然肤色较黑、专横且讽刺，但他把我当作智力上的平等者与我交谈，探索着我的思想，并尊重着我坦诚独立的回答。

paragraphs.en: One night around two o'clock, I was awakened by a demoniacal laugh right outside my bedroom door, followed by a tragic groan. Rushing out, I discovered thick smoke billowing from Mr. Rochester's bedchamber! The curtains were blazing, and Mr. Rochester lay fast asleep in the flames. I dashed water from the pitcher over the bed, saving his life. Awakening in shock, Rochester seized my hands, his dark eyes glowing with intense, unspoken affection.
paragraphs.zh: 一天晚上大约两点钟，我被卧室门外一个恶魔般的笑声惊醒，紧接着是一声悲惨的呻吟。冲出去，我发现浓烟从罗切斯特先生的卧房里涌出！窗帘正在燃烧，而罗切斯特先生在火焰中沉睡。我从水罐里把水泼在床上，救了他的命。在震惊中醒来，罗切斯特紧握着我的双手，他黑色的双眼闪烁着强烈、未曾说出口的真情。

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Party and Blanche Ingram
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 5 章：贵族宴会与布兰切的嫉妒

paragraphs.en: Shortly after the fire, Mr. Rochester left Thornfield for a fortnight, returning with a grand party of wealthy aristocrats, including the beautiful, haughty Miss Blanche Ingram. Mrs. Fairfax informed me that everyone expected Mr. Rochester to marry Miss Ingram for her high birth and beauty. Sitting quietly in the corner of the drawing-room each evening, I watched them with a heavy, aching heart.
paragraphs.zh: 火灾后不久，罗切斯特先生离开桑菲尔德两周，带着一大群富有的贵族归来，包括美丽高傲的布兰切·英格拉姆小姐。费尔法克斯太太告诉我每个人都期望罗切斯特先生因为布兰切的高贵出身与美丽而娶她。每天晚上安静地坐在客厅的角落里，我怀着沉重疼痛的心注视着他们。

paragraphs.en: Yet as I observed Miss Ingram, I realized she was superficial, prideful, and cold, incapable of loving Rochester for who he truly was. One evening, an old gypsy woman arrived at the hall, insisting on reading the fortunes of the young ladies. When I stepped into the room, the disguised gypsy proved to be Mr. Rochester himself! He probed my heart, trying to make me jealous of Blanche, but I maintained my quiet dignity.
paragraphs.zh: 然而当我观察英格拉姆小姐时，我意识到她是肤浅、自大且冰冷的，无法因为罗切斯特真实的自我而爱他。一天晚上，一位老吉普赛妇人来到庄园，坚持要为年轻女士们看相。当步入房间时，伪装的吉普赛人被证明正是罗切斯特先生本人！他探索着我的心，试图让我嫉妒布兰切，但我保持着我安静的尊严。

chapters.title: Chapter 6: The Chestnut Tree Proposal
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 6 章：栗树下的真情告白与求婚

paragraphs.en: On a balmy midsummer eve, I walked alone in the fragrant orchard under the towering chestnut tree. Mr. Rochester joined me, and we walked together in the dusk. He began to speak of his impending marriage to Miss Ingram, suggesting that I must soon leave Thornfield to take a new position in Ireland. At the thought of leaving him forever, tears welled in my eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个温和的仲夏前夕，我独自漫步在高耸栗树下香气扑鼻的果园里。罗切斯特先生加入了我的行列，我们在黄昏中一起漫步。他开始谈论他即将到来的与英格拉姆小姐的婚姻，暗示着我很快必须离开桑菲尔德去爱尔兰接受一个新的职位。一想到要永远离开他，眼泪涌出了我的双眼。

paragraphs.en: 'Do you think, because I am poor, obscure, plain, and little, I am soulless and heartless?' I cried out, my passion breaking all bounds. 'You think wrong! I have as much soul as you—and full as much heart! And if God had gifted me with some beauty and much wealth, I should have made it as hard for you to leave me, as it is now for me to leave you. I am not talking to you now through the medium of custom, conventionalities, nor even of mortal flesh: it is my spirit that addresses your spirit; just as if both had passed through the grave, and we stood at God's feet, equal—as we are!'
paragraphs.zh: “你以为，因为我贫穷、卑微、貌不惊人且矮小，我就没有灵魂也没有心了吗？”我喊道，我的热情冲破了一切防线。“你想错了！我和你一样拥有灵魂——也拥有一模一样完整的心！如果上帝赐予我一些美丽和巨额财富，我会让你离开我像现在我离开你一样艰难。我现在不是通过习俗、惯例、甚至凡俗肉身的中介在和你说话：是我的灵魂在向你的灵魂说话；就像两者都穿过了坟墓，我们站在上帝脚下，平等着——就像我们原本的样子！”

paragraphs.en: 'My bride is here,' Rochester clasped me fiercely in his arms, kissing my lips with passionate devotion. 'Because my equal is here, and my likeness. Jane, will you marry me?' Seeing his sincere tears, I accepted his proposal with boundless joy. That night, a violent storm struck, and lightning split the ancient chestnut tree in two.
paragraphs.zh: “我的新娘在这里，”罗切斯特凶猛地把我紧抱在怀里，带着热情的奉献亲吻着我的双唇。“因为我的平等者在这里，我的相似者在这里。简，你愿意嫁给我吗？”看到他真诚的眼泪，我怀着无尽的喜悦接受了他的求婚。那天晚上，一场剧烈的暴风雨降临，闪电将古老的栗树劈成了两半。

chapters.title: Chapter 7: The Interrupted Wedding and Bertha Mason
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 7 章：被中断的婚礼与阁楼疯女人

paragraphs.en: On a bright summer morning, Rochester and I walked to the quiet parish church for our wedding. But as the clergyman asked if anyone knew of any impediment to our union, a stranger named Mr. Briggs stepped forward, declaring: 'The marriage cannot go on! Mr. Rochester has a wife now living!'
paragraphs.zh: 在一个明亮的夏天早上，罗切斯特和我步入安静的教区教堂举行婚礼。但当牧师询问是否有人知道我们结合的任何阻碍时，一位名叫布里格斯先生的陌生人走上前去，宣布：“婚礼不能继续！罗切斯特先生有一位现活着的妻子！”

paragraphs.en: Rochester grew deathly pale, acknowledging the truth. He led the wedding party back to Thornfield and up to the locked third-floor chamber. Unlocking the door, he revealed a terrifying sight: a wild, monstrous woman with dark hair and a discolored face was pacing the room like a caged beast. It was Bertha Mason, Rochester's mad wife, whom he had been tricked into marrying fifteen years earlier in Jamaica, and who was guarded by Grace Poole.
paragraphs.zh: 罗切斯特面色如死般苍白，承认了真相。他带着婚礼随行人员回到桑菲尔德，上了锁着的三楼房间。打开门锁，他露出了一个可怕的景象：一个狂乱、怪诞的女人带着黑发和变色的面庞正像笼中野兽一样在房间里踱步。那是伯莎·梅森，罗切斯特疯狂的妻子（十五年前他在牙买加被诱骗娶了她），由格雷斯·普尔看守着。

paragraphs.en: Rochester begged me to stay with him as his true wife in spirit, offering to take me to his villa in the south of France. My heart bled for his tragic suffering, but my conscience and self-respect remained unyielding: 'I will keep the law given by God; sanctioned by man. Laws and principles are not for the times when there is no temptation. They are for such moments as this.' That night, while Rochester slept, I packed a small bundle and fled Thornfield into the dark night.
paragraphs.zh: 罗切斯特恳求我留在身边作为他灵魂上真正的新娘，提出带我去他在法国南部的别墅。我的心为他的悲剧痛苦而流血，但我的良知与自尊保持着不可动摇：“我要守住上帝给出的律法；由人类认可的律法。律法与原则不是为了没有诱惑的时刻。它们正是为了像现在这样的时刻。”那天晚上，当罗切斯特入睡时，我收拾了一个小包，在黑夜中逃离了桑菲尔德。

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Moor House and St. John Rivers
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 8 章：沼泽房与圣约翰的求婚

paragraphs.en: Fleeing on a coach until my last penny was spent, I was left wandering helpless on the lonely, desolate moors. For three days I suffered intense hunger, cold, and exhaustion, sleeping on the damp heather and begging for bread at a village doorstep.
paragraphs.zh: 乘坐马车逃跑直到花光最后一分钱，我被留在了孤独荒凉的沼泽上无助地游荡。整整三天我承受着剧烈的饥饿、寒冷与疲惫，睡在潮湿的石楠花上，在村庄门口乞求面包。

paragraphs.en: Collapsing on the doorstep of Moor House, I was rescued by St. John Rivers, a stern young clergyman, and his two gentle sisters, Mary and Diana. They nursed me back to health, and St. John secured a position for me as the schoolmistress of a village school for poor girls. Soon after, St. John discovered that my late uncle in Madeira had left me an inheritance of twenty thousand pounds, and that the Rivers family were my cousins! Overjoyed, I divided the fortune equally among the four of us.
paragraphs.zh: 倒在沼泽房的门口，我被圣约翰·里弗斯（一位严厉的年轻牧师）以及他的两个温柔姐妹玛丽与戴安娜所救。她们把我照顾恢复了健康，圣约翰为我争取到了一个作为贫穷女孩乡村学校女教师的职位。不久之后，圣约翰发现我已故在马德拉的舅舅留给了我两万镑遗产，而且里弗斯家族正是我的表亲！喜出望外，我把财产在四个人中间平分了。

paragraphs.en: St. John, driven by religious fanaticism, proposed that I marry him and accompany him to India as a missionary's wife. He admitted he did not love me, but demanded my obedience. As I hesitated under his intense pressure, I suddenly heard a phantom voice calling out through the night, filled with agony: 'Jane! Jane! Jane!' It was the voice of Edward Rochester.
paragraphs.zh: 圣约翰在宗教狂热的驱使下，提出要我嫁给他并作为传教士的妻子陪同他去印度。他承认他不爱我，但要求我服从。当我在他强烈的压力下犹豫不决时，我突然听到一个幽灵般的声音在夜色中呼唤，充满了痛苦：“简！简！简！”那是爱德华·罗切斯特的声音。

chapters.title: Chapter 9: The Destruction of Thornfield
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 9 章：桑菲尔德庄园的毁灭与烈火

paragraphs.en: Leaving Moor House early the next morning, I traveled post-haste back to Thornfield Hall. But when the carriage rounded the hill, a shocking spectacle met my eyes: Thornfield Hall was a blackened, roofless ruin of charred stone and ashes!
paragraphs.zh: 第二天清晨离开沼泽房，我火速赶回桑菲尔德庄园。但当马车绕过山头时，一个震撼的景象出现在我眼前：桑菲尔德庄园成了一座黑乎乎、没有屋顶的焦石与灰烬废墟！

paragraphs.en: At the local inn, the landlord recounted the tragic story: a few months after my departure, the mad wife Bertha Mason had set fire to my old bedroom. As the flames consumed the mansion, Rochester risked his life to rescue the servants and climbed onto the blazing roof to save Bertha. But she jumped to her death, and the roof collapsed beneath Rochester.
paragraphs.zh: 在当地旅馆，店主讲述了那个悲剧的故事：在我离开几个月后，疯狂的妻子伯莎·梅森纵火烧毁了我原来的卧室。随着火焰吞噬豪宅，罗切斯特冒着生命危险拯救仆人们，并爬上燃烧的屋顶去救伯莎。但她跳楼身亡，屋顶在罗切斯特脚下坍塌。

paragraphs.en: He survived the fall, but was left blind in both eyes and lost his left hand. He now lived in complete solitude and dark melancholy at Ferndean, a secluded manor thirty miles away. My heart overflowed with love and compassion, and I departed immediately for Ferndean.
paragraphs.zh: 他在坠落中幸存下来，但双眼失明并失去了左手。他现在在三十英里外隐蔽的芬丁庄园过着完全孤独与黑暗忧郁的生活。我的心充满了爱与同情，我立刻启程前往芬丁。

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Reader, I Married Him
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 10 章：读者，我嫁给了他（终极幸福）

paragraphs.en: Arriving at Ferndean in the chill evening rain, I saw Edward Rochester stepping out onto the porch, reaching out his hands blindly into the dark. He was rugged, helpless, and broken, yet his noble soul remained. I carried a glass of water to him, and as he touched my hands, he recognized me with a gasp of disbelief: 'Jane! Is it Jane?'
paragraphs.zh: 在寒冷的晚雨中到达芬丁，我看到爱德华·罗切斯特步出走廊，在黑暗中盲目地伸出双手。他身材粗犷、无助且残疾，然而他高尚的灵魂依旧存在。我端着一杯水走向他，当他摸到我的双手时，他带着不敢相信的喘息认出了我：“简！是简吗？”

paragraphs.en: I pressed his sightless head to my bosom, kissing his eyes and hands. I assured him that I was now an independent woman of fortune, and that I would never leave his side again. Rochester wept tears of profound gratitude to God, confessing that on that fateful night, he had called out my name in anguish across the distance.
paragraphs.zh: 我将他失明的头部紧贴在我的胸膛，亲吻着他的双眼与双手。我向他保证我现在是一个拥有财产的独立女性，我再也不会离开他的身边。罗切斯特向上帝流下了深沉感恩的眼泪，承认在那个致命的夜晚，他在远处痛苦地呼唤过我的名字。

paragraphs.en: Reader, I married him. A quiet wedding was celebrated, and we settled into a life of perfect, equal harmony. Two years later, Rochester gradually recovered partial sight in one eye, allowing him to see our firstborn son in his arms. We were blessed with an eternal love built upon mutual respect, spiritual equality, and unshakeable devotion.
paragraphs.zh: 读者，我嫁给了他。举办了一场安静的婚礼，我们落脚在一种完美、平等的和谐生活中。两年后，罗切斯特一只眼睛逐渐恢复了部分视力，使他能够看到抱着我们第一个出生的儿子。我们被赋予了建立在相互尊重、精神平等与不可动摇奉献基础上的永恒之爱。
